findings.detail: 20 cases. THE DIRECT HALF: src/fabric/api.py::_var_cov over n in {1,2,3,5,8} x d in {1,4,16}, requiring BOTH returned tensors finite AND d(var+cov)/dz finite -- the gradient half matters because a finite loss with a NaN gradient is the same poisoning one step later and a check that reads only the loss cannot see it. THE ANALYTIC HALF: at n=1 the variance must equal 1 - sqrt(1e-4) = 0.99 to 1e-6, the covariance exactly 0.0, and dL/dz exactly 0.0. That number is not a recorded float: a single point centres to exactly 0, so its biased variance is 0, std = sqrt(0 + 1e-4) = 0.01, and relu(1 - std) sits at its maximum for ANY single row at ANY width -- which is why 1e-6 is a tolerance on float32 rounding and not on a measurement. THE END-TO-END HALF: two real routed passes at n_live=1, one with the pool full (FAB_N0=1, FAB_SLOTS=1) and one on r_fabric's other reachable arm (FAB_N0=1, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=1.5), each requiring a finite aux_loss and finite dL/dA and dL/dB -- and each asserting fab.ident_trained first, because _ae_loss is _var_cov's only caller and an arm where the round trip did not run proves nothing about it. findings.detail: 4 cases over the third FAB entry point with a body -- the one the brief did not name and that nothing had ever called. THE KIND: manage_period at FAB_MANAGE_EVERY 1, 500 and 0 must return a units.Windows carrying that number, because Config hands back a bare int for every clock-unit lever while RUN's Cadences.due refuses an int, and that is the whole reason the accessor exists. THE NEGATIVE IS ASSERTED AS A PROPERTY OF THE PATH AND NOT OF ONE FILE'S LINE, and this is the part I rewrote mid-round because the tree moved under me. There are now TWO refusals between the environment and a cadence reader, in different packages: spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows (landed by another agent at 23:53 this run) refuses a negative period_windows and runs inside the coupling compute for FAB.d_manage_period, so it fires during spine.assemble.build BEFORE any Config exists; and src/fabric/api.py::manage_period refuses one at its own read under the D4 switch. The check demands what both exist for -- a negative cadence never reaches a reader -- and REPORTS WHICH LAYER REFUSED IT in the detail line, so the day one of them moves the report says so instead of the check going quietly green over the other. It also holds the D4 switch to meaning something in BOTH positions: if nothing refuses and the switch is True, FAB's promise did not bind and it FAILS; if nothing refuses and the switch is False, the answer must be Windows(-5) exactly, because D4 makes OFF the PRE-REFUSAL behaviour and a third answer for one number is the defect the refusal was written to end; and if FAB refuses while the switch is False, the switch does not bind and it FAILS. Zero is held to Windows(0) in every position, because no meaning for 0 is declared for this lever. LOAD-BEARING ACROSS THE WHOLE MATRIX, four mirrors: derive's refusal off with FAB's on -> PASS, and the detail line correctly reports 'the refusal came from FAB.manage_period'; BOTH off -> FAIL, 'FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-5 reached a reader as Windows(-5)'; derive off + switch off -> PASS, 'nothing refused it and manage_period returned Windows(-5)', which is D4's OFF honoured; derive off + switch off + FAB's guard ignoring the switch -> FAIL, 'the switch is the second half of the owner's ruling and it does not bind'.

findings.symbol: src/fabric/api.py::manage_period (its negative-period refusal, and the D4 switch above it)
findings.detail: REFUTES THE SWITCH'S OWN DOCSTRING AS OF THE TREE AT 23:53 TODAY, and it is not a claim I inherited -- I found it because F8 crashed on it. src/fabric/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD says 'False lets the value through to units.Windows exactly as it did before 2026-09-04'. That sentence is now FALSE in both directions: a negative FAB_MANAGE_EVERY cannot reach manage_period at ALL, at either switch position, because spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows now refuses a negative period_windows and it runs inside the coupling compute for FAB.d_manage_period -- i.e. during spine.assemble.build, before any Config exists for manage_period to read. MEASURED: assemble.build with FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=-5 raises UnitError('flush_period_windows: period_windows=Windows(-5) is negative...'); at 0, 1 and 500 it assembles and manage_period returns Windows(0), Windows(1), Windows(500). So FAB's own `if REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD and every < 0:` is UNREACHABLE through the production path, and the D4 switch above it governs a branch nothing can enter. THIS IS NOT A DEFECT IN EITHER REFUSAL -- the value is refused, and refused EARLIER, which is better -- it is a stale sentence and an armed-but-unreachable guard, which is the third DID-IT-FIRE state this project treats as a first-class reading. I did not make F8 fail over it: the property that matters (a negative never reaches a reader) holds, so F8 PASSES and prints which layer did it and that FAB's is unreachable. The fix is a docstring amendment in a file I do not own; it is in unfinished with the exact text.

findings.detail: COST: 2.5 s wall from a cold process, measured three times (2.55 / 2.54 / 2.46 s). 1.51 s of that is `import torch` and 0.62 s is the eight checks together; the slowest single check is F2 at 0.23 s (16 forward passes and 8 backwards) and the cheapest is F8 at under 0.01 s. Nothing here is slow enough to discourage running the suite -- the existing six files are 9.2 s and this takes the suite to 11.8 s, a 28% increase for the first behavioural coverage in the project. The widths are the smallest that still exercise every mechanism (d_model=16, sig_d=12, batch 2, length 4, vocab 11, FAB_N0=4 in a pool of 8, rank and dk at their defaults) against the audits' 32/64/8-of-16, and every effect they measured reproduces. STABILITY: three consecutive runs are BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 0ff4a88b2f2abb100bd3e6558a5bb857 x3). RUN_SEED and RUN_DEVICE are pinned, torch's global seed is set before every population (nn.Linear draws from the global generator), and every input tensor comes from an explicitly seeded torch.Generator.
